question_text: Name one power of the president.
lead_in: Any one of these works (you only need one):

why_it_matters.text: The president wears many hats: signing laws, vetoing bills, leading the military, negotiating treaties, appointing judges. Each role gives the president huge influence — but each one is also balanced by Congress or the courts. That's the system the Founders built so no single person could rule alone.

fun_fact.text: Of all the President's powers, only one has almost no check: to pardon guilty people. Congress can override a veto. The Senate must approve treaties and judges. Courts can rule actions unconstitutional. But the Supreme Court has called the pardon power 'unlimited except in cases of impeachment.'
